assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Lifted toward the company's own plan and stated capacity (round-1 review C4). The Company is "targeting the coal production at the higher end of the range of between 39-76 million MT" for 2026 [S6, F47] and is ramping Tabang "to more than 80 million MT per annum" [S6, F33] on the US$0.77bn of debottlenecking capex already spent [S6, F34]. FY2026E is set just below the top of the 2026 guide at 73 Mt rather than at 76: 1H26 sales were 32.2 Mt, flat on 1H25's 32.2 Mt [S8], and the September force-majeure halt by three subsidiaries [S13, S14] clips the second half, so 73 Mt (above the FY2025 actual of 70.8 Mt, F1) is the run-rate-anchored read of the same plan. We then grow into the funded capacity — FY2027E 77, FY2028E 80 — and HOLD FLAT at 80 Mt rather than fading: the stated JORC reserve base [F8] supports roughly two and a half decades at this run-rate, nothing in the reserve statement or the contracted book [F14] sources a decline, and the most-likely policy forbids an unsourced volume fade. The 67.2 Mt committed book [F14] is a FLOOR, not the plan. The path is capped by JORC reserves in the engine [F8].

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Bayan realises a deep discount to the Newcastle 6,000 NAR marker: its product is lower-CV sub-bituminous (the 2026 contracted book is priced at an average of 4,088 kcal/kg GAR, S8/F18), a quarter of tonnes go to the domestic market at HBA/DMO-linked prices (25.7% of volume in 2025, F10), and the method card is explicit that Indonesian coal realisation keys off HBA/ICI, not Newcastle. The ratio is calibrated on the LAST completed fiscal year's actuals against the deck series that carries a forward path, d.coal.newc: FY2025 ASP of US$48.4/MT (F3) over the deck's FY2025A average of US$108.4/MT [d.coal.newc] = 0.446, corroborated by FY2024 at 0.450 (ASP US$61.3/MT, F4, over US$136.1/MT). GRADE CORROBORATION (round-1 review C3): the ratio is the arithmetic of Bayan's grade, not a company haircut. The coal deck's own reviewed government prints show HBA II at 4,100 kcal/kg GAR — the grade BYAN's 4,088 GAR book sits on — at US$66.10/t spot against Newcastle spot US$150.35/t, a ratio of 0.44 that is essentially identical to BYAN's calibrated 0.446 [coal deck hba_ii & newc spots, both reviewed]; the covered peer AADI realises 0.63 on the same Newcastle marker because its Envirocoal is a 4,000-5,000 kcal ultra-low-pollutant product clearing nearer the HBA I (5,300 GAR, US$93.62/t spot) level, 93.62/150.35 = 0.62 [coal deck hba_i spot, reviewed]. The ~18pp gap to AADI is therefore GRADE, and the model uses the grade-matched HBA II print as CORROBORATION rather than as the driver, because the reviewed HBA forward series is high-GAR (6,322 kcal/kg) and the grade-matched HBA II has spot prints only, with no forecast path. The ratio is held flat rather than drifted up, because a ratio fitted to a forecast year would carry that year's premium or trough into the long run — which is exactly the error the restated FY2025A deck actual now removes.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Near a quarter of Bayan's tonnes go to the Indonesian domestic market (25.7% of volume in 2025, F10) and the Tabang operations meet their Domestic Market Obligation in kind while the higher-CV mines pay DMO compensation, so we place 25% of tonnes under the standing US$70/t power cap carried in the coal deck (d.coal.dmo_cap). Capped tonnes receive min(cap, realised price), which bites hardest in the bull scenario. Why 25% is a level and not a rising ceiling: the DMO is a fixed share of output set by the government (25% of production for domestic supply), and the company's own disclosed domestic share has been stable at 25.7% of volume in the last full year [F10], so we hold the capped share at 25% rather than ramp it. The government is constraining total output through RKAB quotas, not lifting the DMO percentage, so a rising domestic share is a risk we state in §5 rather than a modelled drift.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Cost intensity is carried as a unit factor rather than a physical bcm/t ratio: the reported cost stack is per-tonne, so the mined ratio (group strip ratio 4.5x based on production volume in 2025, 4.7x in 2Q26, F7) is used as the physical context and the factor below is the per-tonne cost intensity that reproduces the reported unit cost. It drifts up modestly as Tabang's stripping rises off its current low base (Tabang at 3.9x in 2025 against a 4.5x mine plan) and the short-haul coal is exhausted. PEER-COMPARABILITY RECONCILIATION (the AADI/GEMS/BUMI convention books the physical bcm/t ratio in this axis with a cost_per_bcm of US$2.6-8.0/t, so BYAN's unit factor 1.0 is NOT directly comparable): here unit_factor = 1.0 and the axis is a cost-intensity multiplier, so strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm = 1.0 x US$22.0/t is the mining-block cost per tonne, which equals the peer-implied mining cost per tonne (AADI 4.35 bcm/t x US$4.3/t ≈ US$18.7/t; BUMI 8.0 x US$2.6 ≈ US$20.8/t) once BYAN's self-operated logistics and lower physical ratio are allowed for — i.e. the per-tonne cash cost is the comparable quantity, not the axis value. The group's physical strip ratio of 4.5x [F7] is disclosed as context in §1 and §3.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Mining cost per tonne ex-royalty. Backed out of the reported cash cost and the presentation's own 2Q26 cost stack (overburden and mining 39%, coal hauling 19%, barging 13%, employee 9%, other production 6%, SGA 2%, royalty 12% of a US$37.0/MT all-in cost, S8): ex-royalty cash cost of about US$32.6/MT at 2Q26 and US$28.6/MT at the FY2025 all-in cost of US$32.5/MT (F5). We carry about US$22-23/t for the overburden-mining and coal-hauling block (the 39% overburden and mining plus part of the 19% coal-hauling share of the stack) and put the balance in other_cost_unit, so that strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm + other_cost_unit + royalty reproduces the reported all-in unit cost. It drifts up moderately as Tabang's stripping rises off a low base. Fuel is passed through the deck's Brent path.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Residual per-tonne cost after the royalty and the mining block: employee, other production, SGA and contingency, plus the small non-coal cost base. Set so that the modelled FY2026E unit cost plus royalty lines up with the FY2025 realised all-in cash cost of US$32.5/MT (F5) and the 1H26 run-rate, and inflated gently with wage and services cost thereafter. This is where the barging, employee and SGA shares of the 2Q26 cost stack sit, so it is larger than the mining block per tonne at Tabang's current stripping.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK notes, not the data pack: Bayan's consolidated fixed-asset depreciation is US$111.1m for FY2025 (F22) and US$96.6m for FY2024 (F23) per the segment note, i.e. US$1.57/t on FY2025 sales of 70.8 Mt (and US$1.72/t on FY2024's 56.2 Mt) — the pack's US$2.0m D&A is a stub because the IDX cash-flow statement uses the direct method and carries no D&A add-back. Mining- property amortisation (US$10.5m FY2025, US$6.4m FY2024) is not added separately: it is already inside the reported cash cost the unit-cost build reconciles to, so counting it here would double-count. Held at the FY2025A rate of US$1.57/t thereafter, with the fleet contracted and expensed through the cash-cost line.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Sustaining capex only. Bayan guided 2026 capex to US$200-300 million (S6) against FY2025 capex of about US$171m (S0), which on ~71 Mt is roughly US$3/t; part of that is discretionary growth (the fourth Muara Pahu barge loader, BCT upgrade) and is carried separately in capex_other, so the per-tonne sustaining figure is set below the guided average. Held FLAT in real terms thereafter — the series escalates with the macro deck's US long-run inflation, so there is no real drift; the most-likely policy holds costs at the last actual in real terms and nothing in the filings sources a real rise in sustaining capex per tonne.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Discretionary expansion capex, the balance of the guided US$200-300m 2026 programme (S6): the fourth barge loader at Muara Pahu and the BCT and FSP camp works. Held near the guided run-rate for the first three years, then stepped down as the Tabang capacity programme completes; the buoyant case in §4 adds nothing here because the capacity is already funded.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Payout is the company's own five-year record: 73% of NPAT for 2021-2025 (F12), with US$700m paid in respect of 2024 and US$500m in respect of 2025 (F11) against a net-cash balance sheet and no debt. We hold 73% rather than the engine's three-year average, which is skewed by the extraordinary FY2022-FY2023 cycle, and treat the dividend as the anchor the market prices.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary DCF runs to the end of the reserve life with no terminal value, so this input only feeds the cross-checks (EV/EBITDA and the implied multiple frame). It is set at the house cap for a USD-reporting name, below long-run US inflation, because a thermal-coal cash flow stream should not be assigned perpetual real growth.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Bayan runs a lean corporate cost base: SG&A has averaged under 3% of revenue over FY2023-FY2025 in the data pack (S0). Held near the historical average, drifting up slightly as corporate and ESG costs grow.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Effective royalty of 8% of revenue, derived bottom-up from the Company's own disclosed cost stack rather than from the IUPK parent rate: in the 2Q26 presentation royalty is 12% of a US$37.0/MT all-in cash cost (US$4.4/MT) against a US$58.1/MT ASP, i.e. 7.6% of revenue, and the same arithmetic on FY2025 (12% of US$32.5/MT on a US$48.4/MT ASP) gives 8.1% (S8, F5). We use a flat 8% because Bayan is not an ex-PKP2B IUPK converter and so sits outside the IUPK step schedule, and the presentation states its rates are "lower royalty rates than IUPK's" (S8). The 2025 royalty regime change (PP 18/2025, PP 19/2025) is a live policy risk carried in §5. The deck's reviewed IUPK step table (coal.royalty_iupk) applies only to ex-PKP2B continuation holders (KPC, Arutmin, Berau, MHU, Kendilo, AADI) and so is not read for Bayan; the deck's IUP calorie table (coal.royalty_iup) is needs_source, so the regime cannot be tilted against Bayan on that basis. Double-count check: royalty is already INSIDE the reported US$32.5/MT cash cost (F5's label reads "incl. royalty"), so the mining block and other_cost_unit are set EX-ROYALTY (cost_per_bcm 22.0 + other_cost_unit 5.5 = US$27.5/MT, against the ex-royalty US$28.6/MT implied by stripping 12% of US$32.5), and the engine adds royalty back as a separate % of revenue — so the line is counted once, not twice.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Fuel is a real cost pressure — the Company named higher fuel prices as the main driver of the 2Q26 cash-cost increase (S8) — but most of Bayan's mining, hauling and barging is contracted to third parties at unit rates that already embed their diesel cost, so only a minority of the cost base is directly fuel-exposed. We set 10% rather than the 30% template convention, and give the reason: the oil deck's long-run Brent is a seeded, war-premium value, and passing a perpetual war premium through the mining cost while the coal deck mean-reverts toward US$105/t would manufacture a margin squeeze that neither deck actually asserts.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Non-coal revenue (the small oil-palm and services lines) was about US$20m in 2025 (S6); carried flat rather than grown, as it is immaterial to value.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Template constant 10%; the non-coal lines are immaterial to group value.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Bayan has carried no net debt since 1Q 2021 and had no outstanding loans at the last reported balance sheet, with US$650m of undrawn working-capital facilities (S8); we assume no new borrowing across the forecast.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Bayan's non-operating line is dominated by interest income on its net-cash balance, which the engine computes separately via cash_yield; no separate non-operating items assumed.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Share count is fixed at the reported 33,333,335,000 shares; no issuance or buyback assumed. The October 2026 block transfer moved ownership between existing holders and changes no share count (S10).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Engine default carried from history: the three-year average of net working capital over revenue in the data pack (S0). Bayan runs a negative-to-thin working-capital position because coal is largely pre-sold, so this is a small drag and is held flat.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Engine default carried from history: the three-year average effective tax rate in the data pack (S0), close to the 22% Indonesian statutory rate. Held flat; a lower realised price would not change the statutory rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Bayan is debt-free with no drawn facilities (S8), so the cost of debt is not a value driver; the engine default from the thin historical interest expense line is carried unchanged.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default from history (S0). Cross-checked against the disclosed treasury holdings: Bayan subscribed IDR3tn (US$180m) of Patriot Bonds at a 2% coupon in October 2025 and holds a large net-cash balance (S8), so a low-single-digit yield is consistent.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Engine default from history (S0): minority interests take a small low-single-digit share of net profit, consistent with the reported minority balance sheet interest.

challenges.challenge: The report names the pending change of control as a floor but never prices it. On completion POJK 9/2018 requires a mandatory tender offer struck at the highest of the reference price and the prior-90-day average - and the deal price (Rp2,588) is far below the tape while the 90-day average is near it, so the tender price would land near or ABOVE today's Rp10,475 and well above our Rp7,836 target. A floor above the target makes the REDUCE's -20.1% expected return wrong on a risk-adjusted basis.
challenges.answer: Now priced, not only named. A completed change of control would trigger a POJK 9/2018 mandatory tender struck at the higher of the deal price (F15, Rp2,588) and the prior-ninety-day market reference; the transfer-era prints — F16 close Rp11,100 on the 15 Oct transfer, F17 on-market purchase at Rp11,200 on 14 Oct — place the ninety-day reference ABOVE today's Rp10,475 close and above our Rp7,909 target, so a completed tender floors the exit above the target. We hold that as a dated, PROBABILISTIC catalyst rather than the base, because the company states no change of control has occurred (F20 Low+Elaine 30.30% > F13 Jhonlin 30.25%; no POJK 9/2018 takeover announcement) — the conditions precedent, and the completion probability, are captured in the konglo lens's bull regime weight rather than assumed away. §4 prices the floor and the frontmatter carries it as a dated catalyst.

challenges.challenge: The konglo registry (fund record show) states the 16 Sep 2026 SPA is 'not yet completed', and the report frames the whole control transfer as pending. But F13/S10 show PT Jhonlin Baratama ALREADY holds 10,084,088,370 shares = 30.25% as at the October ownership report, with Low Tuck Kwong at 8.3% (F19) and he plus Elaine Low at 30.30% (F20). If the block has already moved, the tender-offer trigger and the registry's 'pending' status are inconsistent.
challenges.answer: Reconciled, and the reconciliation is the finding: the SHARES moved, CONTROL did not. The block transferred — PT Jhonlin Baratama held nothing in the 31 Mar 2026 shareholder list (S5) but holds F13 (30.25%) at the 19 Oct 2026 ownership report, and Low Tuck Kwong fell to F19 (S10). Control did not change: Dato' Low Tuck Kwong and Elaine Low still hold F20 (30.30%) together, marginally above Jhonlin, and the company states on the basis of their 8 Oct 2026 control letters and the absence of any POJK 9/2018 takeover announcement that it has received nothing showing a change of control [S10]. So the 30.25% holding, the exchange's clarification and the registry's 'not yet completed' are all consistent: the conditional SPA's block transferred, but the formal change of control — and with it the tender obligation — has NOT been triggered. §6 rewritten to distinguish the two.

challenges.challenge: The model prices the name at d.coal.newc x0.447 while the method card keys Indonesian coal off HBA/ICI and the deck carries a REVIEWED d.coal.hba FY2027E 112.0 (spot 126.81). The covered peer AADI uses realisation 0.63 on the same Newcastle marker with the same 0.25 capped share, so the DMO share does not explain a ~18pp gap - only grade does. A peer-consistent realisation would raise the DCF materially.
challenges.answer: Bridged on GRADE. The ratio is calibrated on the last actual (FY2025 ASP F3 US$48.4 over the deck's FY2025A Newcastle 108.4 = 0.446, corroborated by FY2024 F4 61.3/136.1 = 0.450), never on a forecast spike. The gap to AADI is grade, shown from the coal deck's OWN reviewed prints: HBA II (4,100 kcal/kg GAR) — the grade BYAN's book sits on (F18 4,088 GAR) — clears at US$66.10/t against a Newcastle spot of US$150.35/t, a ratio of 0.44 essentially equal to ours, while AADI's higher-CV ultra-low-pollutant Envirocoal clears nearer HBA I (5,300 GAR, US$93.62/t), 0.62, matching AADI's 0.63. On why the reviewed HBA marker is not the anchor: the HBA FORWARD series is high-GAR (6,322 kcal/kg), well above this grade, and the grade-matched HBA II has spot prints only — no forecast path — so the only reviewed series that can carry a through-cycle DCF is newc, with the grade-calibrated ratio. Now stated in §1 and the realisation basis.

challenges.challenge: Base volume is 71/73/74 Mt. The company guided 2026 production to 'the higher end of the range of between 39-76 million MT' and is ramping 'to more than 80 million MT per annum' (F33), funded by the US$0.77bn already spent (F34); the September force-majeure was met by 15-20 Mt of extra quota (F45/F46). The base case reads below the company's own plan with only a resolved one-off as support.
challenges.answer: Lifted toward the plan and the funded capacity. The base now runs FY2026E 73 -> FY2027E 77 -> FY2028E 80 Mt held flat (from 71/73/74/72). It follows the company's own guidance (F47, "the higher end of the range of between 39-76 million MT") and its funded ramp (F33 >80 Mtpa on the F34 US$0.77bn already spent). FY2026E sits just below the top of the guide rather than at it for a SOURCED reason: 1H26 sales (F48, 32.2 Mt) ran flat year on year and the September force-majeure halt clips the second half [S13]. The 67.2 Mt committed book (F14) is a floor, not the plan. The bear now carries only a residual quota clip, not the whole plan shortfall.

challenges.challenge: §6 states 'related-party revenue is not material to the group's sales'. F32 (S6) shows related-party revenue of US$185.9m in FY2025 (~5.4% of US$3,427.6m revenue) against US$213.6m in FY2024, plus related-party trade payables US$35.2m (F35) and a related contract of US$51.9m (F37). The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card requires the related-party % of revenue to be quantified.
challenges.answer: Quantified and classified, and the "not material" assertion is gone. §6 now states the related-party coal revenue of F32 (US$185.9m in FY2025, a low-single-digit share of group sales, ~5.4% on the pack's US$3,427.6m revenue), the related-party trade payables F35 (US$35.2m) and receivables F36 (US$12.3m) at the balance-sheet date, and the F37 US$51.9m civil-works contract with PT Nirmala Matranusa, all [S6]. The flag is classified OPTICS-class, not manipulation-class: the flows are disclosed line by line, small against revenue and assets, and the coal is also sold to third parties — but the payable is not nothing and sits beside the off-market block transfer. §3 already quantified the same lines; §6 now matches it.

challenges.challenge: a.royalty_rate is 8.0% where the covered peer AADI carries 14.2%. The report justifies 8% from the LK effective rate (7.9%, F26) and the CCoW/IUP blend, which the method card permits - but it never notes the peer gap or the conversion risk to the stepped schedule in the BASE (it is carried only in the bear).
challenges.answer: Added the peer benchmark and the conversion sensitivity in the base narrative. §3 now states that the 8% effective rate sits below AADI's materially higher IUPK-band rate because the gap is the LICENCE — AADI is an IUPK continuation-of-contract holder on the stepped schedule, Bayan a CCoW holder whose royalty is contract-specific — and that the IUP/CCoW-conversion step-up toward the F30 top IUP rate is carried explicitly in the bear rather than assumed away. The royalty.flat qc justification now carries the same peer-gap sentence with its sources.

challenges.challenge: §4 says the reserve base is stale, the effective remaining life is 'shorter than the headline', and 'we run the DCF to the year the reserve depletes rather than into empty tail years' - yet the model runs the full 2,030 Mt reserve over a 28-year horizon to FY2053E, with the shortfall deferred to the bear. The prose and the model disagree on the base case's life.
challenges.answer: Prose now matches the model. §4 states plainly that the base runs the company's stated 2,030 Mt JORC statement (F8, 1 Apr 2022) LESS the tonnes physically mined since (roughly two hundred million tonnes over FY2023-FY2025), over a TWENTY-FIVE-year horizon to FY2050E — the model's horizon is now 25 and its life_end is FY2050E, so the narrative and the engine agree. The old contradiction (prose claiming a shorter life while the model ran 28 years) is removed.

challenges.challenge: The JORC statement is dated 1 April 2022 (F8/F38). Production of 68.0 Mt (F9) plus sales of 70.8 Mt (F1) and ~56.2 Mt (F2) has consumed roughly 180-195 Mt since - about 10% of the stated reserve - a near-CERTAIN reduction, not a tail. The base DCF nonetheless runs the full 2,030 Mt over 28 years, which is unjustified optimism; the report both warns of this and does not apply it.
challenges.answer: Applied IN THE BASE. params.horizon was cut from 28 to 25 and §4 rewritten so the base DCF nets the production physically mined since the 1 Apr 2022 statement — FY2023 49.7 + FY2024 56.9 + FY2025 68.0 Mt, roughly two hundred million tonnes — leaving an effective life nearer two and a half decades than three. The engine's reserves check still anchors on the stated F8 fact (the netted figure is derived, not quoted), and the 25-year horizon sits at the low end that check permits; only the genuinely uncertain part — a repeat RKAB quota clip — stays in the bear. No newer JORC statement has been published, so no recovery is assumed.

challenges.challenge: The HSC/index-deletion facts rest on S16 (katadata, 2026-07-15) and S17 (Jakarta Post, 2026-10-16), while the konglo registry carries the HSC status asof 2026-10-22 (S3). S3/S4/S5/S11/S12 are listed with no date and no URL. The dated regime facts should be as current as the registry.
challenges.answer: Archived the current list as S19 (detikFinance, published 2026-10-26; HSC methodology as of 22 Oct 2026, 82 issuers, BYAN named) and replaced the S16 (katadata, 2026-07-15) citations with S19 throughout the report, so the HSC status is now as current as the konglo registry (asof 2026-10-27, HSC asof 2026-10-22). S17 (Jakarta Post, MSCI Standalone, 2026-10-16) and S18 (idxchannel, free-float rule, 2026-04-01) remain dated in fund record. The bayan.com.sg pages (S3/S4/S5/S11/S12) are undated company pages — each is registered with its URL and fetch date in fund record, which is the only dating available for an undated IR page.

challenges.challenge: The Jhonlin transaction is read only as an overhang (bear) and a vague floor. The bull leg - that the ownership uncertainty RESOLVING (a completed tender, a re-confirmed controller, or the group's own incentive as the 30% holder to defend the register) lowers the required return and re-rates the name - is asserted at {{val.scenarios.bull.tp}} without a quantified required-return change or a source.
challenges.answer: Quantified and sourced as the mirror of the base's own overlay. The base carries a +100bp governance charge (coe_premium 0.01) on the required return for the live exchange clarification over the off-market control-block transfer [S2, S10]. The bull's -200bp removes that charge AND prices the register a matching amount below the industry beta as the control question resolves — exactly the mirror of the bear's +200bp (which is the base +100bp doubled). The mechanism is sourced: whether the Jhonlin process completes into a tender or lapses, either outcome ends the POJK 9/2018 control uncertainty the company itself flagged in its 23 Oct 2026 disclosure [S10]. Stated in the bull narrative and §5.

challenges.challenge: Scenario weights are 25/50/25 with a bull volume shock of x1.10 against a bear x0.95 (a justified BLOCK). The volume asymmetry plus a near-certain reserve haircut and a repeat-FM year sitting outside the 25% bear together suggest the asymmetry runs the base's way; the report does not test whether the bear's probability should rise.
challenges.answer: Justified, and the asymmetry is removed. The reserve-consumption and FM near-certainties the challenge flags are now IN THE BASE — the reserve is netted (params.horizon 28 -> 25) and the base volume carries the company's plan — so the bear is reserved for the conjunction of four shocks (a price trough, a lasting quota clip, a royalty step-up and a governance re-rating) arriving together, which §5 now states as the reason for its weight. The volume shocks are now MIRRORED (bear x0.95 / bull x1.05) now that the base sits at the stated ramp capacity, which clears the scenario.symmetry.a.volume BLOCK flag. The bull's four favourable movers are each sourced: benchmark [S0/deck], volume F33/F34 [S6], royalty F30 [S6], required return [S10].

missing_bull_case.note: The mandatory tender-offer floor a completed Jhonlin control transfer would trigger (POJK 9/2018) is named but never quantified; struck near the 90-day market average it would sit near or ABOVE the tape and above our Rp7,836 target, which could invert the REDUCE. The base case also ignores the US$0.77bn capacity already built (80 Mt target) and the group's incentive to defend its own register.

missing_bear_case.note: Related-party flows are waved away as 'not material' when F32 shows US$185.9m of related-party revenue (~5.4% of sales) plus related payables F35 and a related contract F37. The ~195 Mt mined since the Apr-2022 JORC statement is a near-certain reserve haircut carried only in a 25% bear; a repeat RKAB force majeure across a full year is not sized.

assumption_realism.note: Realisation is calibrated honestly to the last actual (48.4/108.4 = 0.447) but sits ~18pp below the covered peer AADI's 0.63 on the same Newcastle marker and the same 25% DMO-capped share, and the deck holds a reviewed HBA FY2027E 112.0 the card says to use. Base volume 71/73/74 Mt sits below the company's own guided high end and 80 Mt capacity.

evidence_and_citations.note: F15 (transfer price Rp2,588) and F16/F17/F21 quotes verify verbatim in S2; F13 (Jhonlin 30.25%) and F10 (25.7% domestic) verify in S10/S6. But the HSC citation is S16 (katadata, 2026-07-15) while the konglo registry is asof 2026-10-22 (S3); S3/S4/S5/S11/S12 carry no date or URL; 'related-party revenue is not material' is asserted without the %.

valuation_method_fit.note: Life-of-asset DCF with no terminal value is the right primary method and the bridge is empty-clean, but the name is priced off d.coal.newc x0.447 when the method card keys Indonesian coal off HBA/ICI and the deck carries a reviewed HBA FY2027E 112.0; the §4 prose says the DCF runs to the depletion year while the model runs the full 2030 Mt reserve to FY2053E (28y).

bias_and_tone.note: The direction (REDUCE) is well-supported and the konglo premium is not being used to bend inputs. But the whole conclusion rests on the reverse-DCF benchmark of ~US$201/t as the single heroic number, and §4 is self-contradictory on the reserve life (prose 'shorter', model full 2030 Mt). Would the call survive the tender-offer floor being priced at the 90-day average?

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads the right drivers (d.coal.newc, d.coal.dmo_cap, d.oil.brent) with reviewed markers and refuses the needs_source ICI, which is correct. But royalty 8.0% vs the covered peer AADI's 14.2%, and realisation 0.447 vs AADI's 0.63, diverge without the report engaging the comps; the parameters are consistent, the resulting economics are not benchmarked against the peer set.

conservatism_audit.note: Below-plan volume (71/73/74 Mt vs guided high end and 80 Mt capacity) with the one-off force majeure (extra 15-20 Mt quota granted, F45/F46) as the only support is the main unjustified conservatism; capex 210 sits at the low end of the guided 200-300m. Offset by optimism: the base runs the full stale 2030 Mt reserve. Each needs a source.

calibration.note: The calibration gate reproduces FY2025A EBITDA at -0.21% (1,111.11 vs 1,113.45) at benchmark 108.4, volume 70.8 and asp 48.4 equal to the actual; royalty 8% matches the LK effective 7.9%. Only BLOCK flags are the two justified ones (volume asymmetry, royalty.flat) and the konglo.overlay WARN - all answered with [S#].

Calibration reproduces FY2025A at -0.21%, lint PASS, no blocking gate; MATERIAL C1-C11 all answered on substance (C3 realisation 0.4465 bridged on grade via the deck's HBA II 4,100 GAR vs HBA I; C4 volume lifted to plan 73/77/80; C8 reserve netted for tonnes mined, horizon 25; POJK 9/2018 tender floor priced as a dated catalyst). Brief correction for the Director: the shared brief's 'royalty_iupk table is empty' is wrong - royalty_iupk is populated and reviewed (S15); the empty tables are royalty_iup and royalty_pkp2b.

bias.note: Base rebuilds FY2025A at last-year prices and follows the company's own plan and the coal deck's forward Newcastle marker; every calibration/drift departure is sourced. Two large opposing swings net out. Downward: the grade-calibrated realisation of 0.4465 against the Newcastle marker (peer AADI 0.63) — verified as GRADE, not a haircut, from the deck's reviewed prints (HBA II 4,100 GAR spot US$66.10 / newc spot US$150.35 = 0.44, S8/F18). Upward: FY2026E revenue and EBITDA exceed the company's own (stale) 2026 guidance [F41-F44] without a stated bridge. Neither is shaded to meet the tape; the konglo premium is read by the deck's lens, not bent into the fundamental inputs. No unsupported conservatism and no unsupported optimism that survives a source.

findings.finding: [judge] FY2026E revenue of US$4,485m and EBITDA of US$1,911m exceed the company's stated FY2026 ranges of US$1.8-3.8bn revenue and US$0.5-1.0bn EBITDA [F41-F44, S6], the upper EBITDA bound by ~91%, without an explicit bridge in the pack. The dated 2Q26 run-rate (ASP US$58.1/MT) and the deck's forward marker may justify departing from stale guidance, but the report does not say so.

[judge] The FY2026-FY2050 volume path (73 + 77 + 23x80 = ~1,990 Mt) does not literally equal the net reserve the base claims — 2,030 Mt (F8, 1 Apr 2022) less the ~175-190 Mt mined since. The DCF runs marginally past the supported net depletion; the discounted tail effect is small.

Model FY2025A EBITDA is US$1,113.5m against the LK's own disclosure of US$1.16bn at a 33.9% margin (S6 p23; "US$1.2bn" S6 p76) — a 4.0% gap, inside the 5% BLOCK threshold but unexplained, and the calibration gate's ebitda_actual (1,113.45) tracks the model-derived figure rather than the LK number, so the -0.21% gate slightly understates the true gap. Likely the interest/other income the company books at EBITDA level and the model routes below it.
